account: Today’s town business has been quiet: the secretary reports no pending correspondence, petitions, accounts, or verified unusual news. What stands out is the lighting and tomorrow’s gathering. Builder requested an eighteen-hundred great hall inspection of newly installed lanterns, calling it routine and saying there was no particular problem. Neighbour independently invited me to the hall at exactly that time and offered to walk with me, later confirming it was the same occasion builder arranged. Neighbour also mentioned cheerful new lights at the bakery, supposedly just to brighten it. This evening I can see numerous lanterns around the plaza and builder nearby carrying a lantern. These details make me wonder whether the lighting work and the shared invitation conceal some coordinated gathering or preparations beyond an ordinary inspection. That is only a suspicion: I have not witnessed a secret meeting or learned any definite hidden purpose. Builder and neighbour are the people directly connected to tomorrow’s event; the secretary has recorded it and clarified my regular tea appointment, but has reported no unusual observations. Freight was carrying bread outside town hall; I asked about dock trade, but have heard no reply, so I cannot connect that to anything. For now, the stated purpose is a routine lighting inspection, and I should ask builder about its details and attendance rather than assume more.
